title: Numbered and Lettered Notes

illustrates.quote: Asterisks, daggers, and double daggers that appear raised from the baseline are not considered to be in the superscript position. (See UEB, §3.3.1, Asterisk, Dagger, and Double Dagger.) Retain the superscript format for all other symbols.

blocks.features: Single print line with a superscript numeral 1 after "script" and a superscript letter a after "libretto".

print.surroundingText: Last of the four reference-mark illustrations directly below rule 16.2.2c; followed by a cross-reference to Sample 16-1: Multiple Reference Marks on page 16-17.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box, one print line only: "script" with superscript "1", the word "or", then "libretto" with superscript "a".

braille.notes: Superscripted number 1 is ;9#a (grade-1 indicator, numeric indicator, letter a for digit 1); superscripted letter a is ;9a (grade-1 indicator then the letter itself, no numeric indicator since it is a letter not a digit).

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.2.2.c per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: no page/line-number evidence; both runs agree, left null. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
